subject: desert ghost town
title: What If a Diamond Town Was Swallowed by Sand? Kolmanskop Was

scenes.text: What if the desert took back a whole town? In Namibia, it started with one diamond.
1908. Railway worker Zacharias Lewala picks a diamond out of the sand. A German town rises ten kilometres from the coast.
Kolmanskop got the southern hemisphere's first X-ray machine, a ballroom, a theatre and Africa's first tram.
The tram brought every home a case of soda, a case of lemonade and a block of ice. Daily. Free.
Then the field ran thin and richer diamonds turned up elsewhere. In 1956 the last people left. The desert didn't.
Today dunes pour through the doorways and tourists wade knee-deep in sand across the ballroom floor. The desert waited. Then it moved back in.

description:
What if the desert swallowed a town? Kolmanskop, Namibia, boomed after railway worker Zacharias Lewala found a diamond in 1908: it got a hospital with the southern hemisphere's first X-ray machine, a ballroom, a theatre, an ice factory and Africa's first tram, which delivered free soda, lemonade and ice daily.
When the diamond field thinned and richer finds appeared elsewhere, the town was abandoned in 1956; today visitors walk through its houses knee-deep in sand.
